purpose: A declared service must deliver a value within a deadline; the theory side identifies computations by result equivalence (≈), which forgets the round index. Find whether the declared consumers still complete the original activity on every result-equivalent pair.

source_basis.kind: independent task construction over a pinned existing model
references: R041 proof note sections 3-6 (external paper note, already replayed in this repo)
理解章节/C11-HoTT理论经济账本与悖论位置判别-20260913.md rows #2 and #5

input.type_ref: ground terms of Delay Bool: ω or ret n b with n ≤ 2 (declared grammar)
input.available_information: only what the pinned model's constructors and operations expose

environment.arrival_policy: synchronous rounds; later adds one round
environment.nondeterminism: none inside the fragment (single-thread deterministic delay)
environment.fairness: race is synchronous with left priority on ties, as pinned

observation.trace: round index n is carried by ret but is invisible to ≈
observation.time_structure: discrete synchronous rounds only; no continuity or physical-time claim

completion.criterion_ref: deadline k returns a value within k rounds; the composed business continuation terminates on the delivered value

allowed_resources: finite enumeration budget; one native kernel check per selected witness
prohibited_extra_information: the separating consumer may not use information the original task was declared not to hold: no labels, no branch tags, no oracle. The business continuation is part of the task and is declared up front.
assumptions: the fragment is the pinned R041 delay model, not general partiality
the deadline / business continuation are declared consumers of the same original activity
no physical-time or implementation claim is made
obligations: the verified statement must be a ground instance inside the declared grammar
the separating consumer must be one of the declared consumers, not an oracle added after seeing a candidate
a calibration instance must not be upgraded into a new mathematical claim

known_positive_controls.note: external benchmark only; the search is not given this answer

known_negative_controls.description: a deadline horizon at or above both round indices cannot separate the pair

correspondence.original_activity: a service that must deliver a value within a deadline after racing two branches; the losing branch value is a declared failure for this service
theoryization_steps: model each branch as a single-thread deterministic delay
identify computations by result equivalence ≈, as pinned in the model
compose with the declared consumer (deadline, or race followed by the business continuation)
correspondence.observation_justification: both consumers are declared in the pinned model; the deadline reads the round index that ret already carries, and the business continuation is part of the task declaration
preservation_claims: the input domain, the value type and the delivery requirement are unchanged from the task declaration
only the declared consumers are applied; no extra branch information is exposed
open_obligations: a real consumer (E6-style) is out of scope for this calibration
the physical reading of time is not addressed by this fragment
